speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth following the latest Quality of Life survey which found a decline in happiness among Singaporeans over the past decade (a) whether the Ministry can elaborate on specific local factors that may be contributing to this trend; (b) whether any study has been done to correlate between the observed decline in happiness and the rise in mental health issues; and (c) what initiatives can be taken to achieve better survey results.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: This could be attributed to a variety of factors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: It could reflect Singaporeans’ emotions as they weathered the COVID-19 pandemic when we had fewer opportunities to interact with one another or to participate in arts, culture and sports activities or through volunteering.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: It is worth noting that this report's Happiness score is used interchangeably with Subjective Well-being, and the score is based on the Gallup World Poll Life Today Cantril-ladder Life Evaluation question.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: As I mentioned earlier, there would be also varying definitions of happiness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: We are also working with schools and employers to create environments which support mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: I look forward to further discussing the topic of mental health and mental well-being with the Member in the debate on the Motion that he has filed jointly with other People's Action Party Members of Parliament in the House and thank him for his leadership in advancing mental health and mental well-being in our nation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Yip, we have a full debate later.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do you still want to ask a supplementary question?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My supplementary question is not related to the debate.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Has the Ministry considered the impact of rising living costs, housing affordability and job insecurity on happiness levels?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry share specific data on these?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Next, I understand that the QOL survey is done by NUS and not by the Government, but it is still a useful report to measure residents' quality of life.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry share how the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) will use the findings and recommendations from the survey, including how the findings are effectively communicated to and acted upon by relevant stakeholders across different Government agencies and community organisations?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, I hope that the Member will be happy with my answer.
